children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session as AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

Zooming in on Amtech

Amtech’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 74 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Amtech and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 7 days ago when the stock dropped 6% on the news that accelerating annual wholesale inflation pushed Treasury yields higher, while executive turmoil at Nvidia pressured chipmakers.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that October’s producer price index rose 0.3% month on month. That was marginally below the 0.4% increase expected by economists polled by Dow Jones, CNBC reported. However, unadjusted final demand climbed 6.5% over the past twelve months, the fastest annual pace since November 2022, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield up nearly four basis points to 5.14%.

Northlight Asset Management Chief Investment Officer Chris Zaccarelli told CNBC that persistent price pressures keep the Federal Reserve on course to raise interest rates in December. When benchmark bond yields sit above 5%, elevated equity valuations face immediate discount-rate pressure.

Amtech is down 16.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $10.86 per share, it is trading 54.7% below its 52-week high of $23.99 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Amtech’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,027.
